THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT Heard Smt.Sharada Patil Kulgeri, learned counsel for the appellants as well as Smt.Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.

Despite service of notice none appears for respondent No.1.
2.

Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Kalaburagi in M.V.C.No.799/2017 dated 02.04.2019.
This is a claimants' appeal.

On the ground their son - Ganesh died in a road traffic accident and that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver - first respondent, the appellants filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.14,25,000/-.
The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- as compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is preferred.
4. Arguing the matter Smt.Sharada Patil Kulgeri, learned counsel for the appellants submits that the deceased - Ganesh was aged about eight years by the date of accident.

He was hale and healthy and Rangamma And Anr vs Jalaluddin And Anr on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18236600/
2 was going to school by the date of accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Due to untimely death of their son, the appellants are put to much hardship and sufferance.
Though their claim is appreciated by the Tribunal, however it awarded a meager sum as compensation and therefore the present appeal is preferred.

Learned counsel, stating that a higher sum ought to have been awarded, relies upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kishan Gopal and others vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 AIR SCW 5037.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and others vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 AIR SCW 5037
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the decision that is relied upon, their Lordships dealing with the cases of similar in nature, held as follows:-
"In our considered view, the aforesaid legal principle laid down in Lata Wadhwa's case with all fours is applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case in hand having regard to the fact that the deceased was 10 years' old, who was assisting the appellants in their agricultural occupation which is an undisputed fact.

We have also considered the fact that the rupee value has come down drastically from the year 1994, when the notional income of the non- earning member prior to the date of accident was fixed at Rs.15,000/-.
Further, the deceased boy, had he been alive would have certainly contributed substantially to the family of the appellants by working hard.

In view of the aforesaid reasons, it would be just and reasonable for us to take his notional income at Rs.30,000/- and further taking the young age of the parents,
namely the mother who was about 36 years old, at the time of accident, NC:
2024:KHC-K:2970 by applying the legal principles laid down in the case of Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [(2009) 6 SCC 121], the multiplier of 15 can be applied to the multiplicand.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [(2009) 6 SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, 30,000 x 15 = 4,50,000 and 50,000/- under conventional heads towards loss of love and affection, funeral expenses, last rites as held in Kerala SRTC v. Susamma Thomas [(1994) 2 SCC 176], which is referred to in Lata Wadhwa's case and the said amount under the conventional heads is awarded even in relation to the death of children between 10 to 15 years old

entities.text: Kerala SRTC v. Susamma Thomas [(1994) 2 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: . In this case also we award Rs.50,000/- under conventional heads.
In our view, for the aforesaid reasons the said amount would be fair, just and reasonable compensation to be awarded in favour of the appellants.

The said amount will carry interest at the rate of 9% p.a. by applying the law laid down in the case of Municipal Council of Delhi v.
Association of Victims of Uphaar Tragedy [(2011) 14 SCC 481], for the reason that the Insurance Company has been contesting the claim of the appellants from 1992- 2013 without settling their legitimate claim for nearly about 21 years, if the Insurance Company had awarded and paid just and reasonable compensation to the appellants the same could have been either invested or kept in the fixed deposit, then the amount could have earned five times more than what is awarded today in this appeal.

sentences.text: Therefore, NC: 2024:KHC-K:2970 awarding 9% interest on the compensation awarded in favour of the appellants is legally justified.

sentences.text: 3 I) The appeal is allowed and the impugned judgments and awards of both the Tribunal and High Court are set aside.
II) The awarded amount of Rs.5,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum should be paid to the appellants from the date of filing of the application till the date of payment.

III) We direct the Insurance Company to issue the demand draft drawn on any Nationalized Bank by apportioning the compensation amount equally with proportionate interest and send it to the appellants within six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment."
6.
Smt.Sharada Patil Kulgeri seeks the court to dispose of the appeal on merits.
7. It is not in dispute that the deceased - Ganesh lost his life at the age of eight years in a road traffic accident.
Also there is no dispute of the fact that the deceased - Ganesh was hale and healthy by the date of NC: 2024:KHC-K:2970 accident.
The mental agony the appellants would have suffered and are suffering cannot be equated to any amount.
Basing on the ratio laid down in the case which is referred supra, this Court is of the view that just compensation that can be awarded is Rupees Five Lakhs.

In the light of the foregoing discussion, the following :
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.

ii) The amount awarded as compensation by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Kalaburgi through orders in M.V.C.No.799/2017 dated 02.04.2019 is enhanced from Rupees Two Lakh to Rupees Five Lakh.
iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till date of deposit.
iv) The second respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:2970 v) Out of the enhanced sum, the first appellant being the mother is entitled to Rupees Two Lakh and the second appellant being the father is entitled to Rupees One Lakh.
vi) The appellants are permitted to withdraw their respective shares along with interest immediately after deposit.
